To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-terminus of H2B plays an important role in chromatin compaction, which is required for SIRT binding and the subsequent establishment of telomere heterochromatin.
the C-terminus of H2B, which is involved in nucleosome-nucleosome interactions, is required for heterochromain assembly in yeast.
the C-terminal tail of H2B, in addition to its ubiquitylation, is required for heterochromatization at telomeres, and that this process is mediated by the Sir complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the histone H2A/H2B heterodimer in chromatin folding and gene silencing in yeast, and has identified the C-terminus of H2B as a novel factor that regulates the compaction of nucleosome array.
the mechanism of heterochromatin establishment and maintenance in budding yeast.
the role of the H2B C-terminal tail in chromatin structure and gene regulation, and has revealed a novel function for the H2B tail in the formation of heterochromatin at telomeres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H2B C-terminal domain is required for the formation of a properly compacted chromatin that is necessary for the establishment of heterochromatin at telomeres.
the compaction and the accessibility of chromatin are two distinct and independent features of the nucleosomal structure.

the H2B C-terminal tail is involved in the formation of a compact chromatin structure that is essential for SIR binding to telomeres, and that this binding is independent of the monoubiquitylated state of H2B at K123.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the compaction state of nucleosomes per se is not enough for the formation of heterochromatin, but the proper arrangement of chromatin mediated by histone H2Bs C-terminus and H2B K-123 ubiquitylation is required for SIRT binding and the formation of telomere heterochromatin.
the compaction per se is not enough for telomeric heterchromatin assembly, instead, the compaction of the nucleosome mediated by H2A/H2B dimer is essential.
the C-terminus of H2B, in addition to its ubiquitylation at lysine 123, is required for heterochromation formation at telomeres, which is independent of SIR proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminus of H2B plays a crucial role in the compaction of nucleosomal arrays at telomeres.
the compaction and the structure of chromatin per-se are not sufficient to induce gene silencing.

the compaction per se of chromatin is not sufficient to induce heterochromatin, but that an appropriately array of nucleosome is required for SIRT binding, which in turn is required for telomeric chromation formation.
